assessments.reasoning: The first-party HTML is a descriptive edition-and-identity source. Its Definitions section and linked source descriptions identify both editions and distinguish the revised edition by name and year.

Physical pages 2 and 3 of the exact book identify the revised title, authors, MIT Press and the 1997 imprint. This is contextual corroboration for only the revised branch. The Standard ML Family source supplies the scope of the two-definition identity statement.

challenge.method: I compared the project’s Definitions section to the separately acquired 1990 definition, the 1997 revised imprint, and the project’s separate links for the Basis Library and Successor ML.
challenge.results: The distributor expressly labels the original and revised language definitions SML ’90 and SML ’97. The revised title page and 1997 imprint corroborate the second identification. The library and evolving derived definition appear as separate subjects.

limitations: The MIT Press metadata route returned HTTP 403, while the exact revised book was directly reacquired through its permissioned project distributor. The 1990, library and Successor ML texts are comparison context.
